svg.text: FIT · PE · PART 4.2 — CHOOSING YOUR ANCILLARIES
Within a family, every member does the same job. You choose by side-effects, half-life,
selectivity, interactions, and what each one also does.
SAME SOCKET, DIFFERENT SKIRT — choose by: side-effects · half-life · selectivity · interactions · also-does · already-handled
the single most useful split in the entire ancillary world
liver-selective · barely enters muscle · most potent
⚑ WATER-SOLUBLE = GENTLER ON MUSCLE. “Rosuva is fat-soluble”? Backwards.
+ EZETIMIBE: close the OTHER door, dose LOW
renal-protective · re-seat with tadalafil once penetration is covered
weakest, unless you are also fighting uric acid
REDUNDANCY DIMMER: GLP-1 seated → telmisartan's PPAR-γ greys to NICE-TO-HAVE
selective · no gyno · the clean pick
blocks androgen receptors → gyno → sabotages your cycle
INTERLOCK: do NOT stack MRA + ARB + thiazide unsupervised (potassium / dehydration)
β1 + NO factory · the heart-rate lever for creeping RHR
ankle-edema masks steroid water · indapamide is NOT a get-drier tool
NO pathway: nebivolol = factory, tadalafil = dam (same axis, opposite ends)
GH-resistance · dose AWAY from training (AMPK ⊣ mTOR)
calorie-dump + BP/water + cardio-renal — best on a cut
PPAR-γ partitioning is seductive, but fluid masks conditioning
retatrutide manages glucose centrally → sidesteps the AMPK/mTOR muscle-blunt
on-cycle PROTECTION — GH burns through your own thyroid
aggressive fat-loss is Part 4.3, not protection
protection seats T4; T3 is a cutting tool, a different job
THE ONE PLACE SELECTION IS ADDITIVE — these stack, they don't compete
for existing gyno (> tamoxifen, a PCT tool)
Test-derived loss ONLY · useless vs DHT-derivatives (Mast/Primo/Winny)
topical route for DHT-derivatives · research chem (transparency, not endorsement)
ORAL MINOXIDIL rewrites your BP stack → ARB + nebivolol become non-negotiable
DEFEND THE SYSTEM, NOT THE DRUG
In a stack, risks MULTIPLY. Protect each system against the COMBINED load: fewer, multi-tasking,
well-chosen parts. The number is still the boss: if BP/HR keep climbing, lower the DOSE, don't add a part.
this tray cabinet is the PROTECTIVE toolbox
spironolactone: picking wrong inside a class can sabotage you.
Almost every agent here is a prescription medicine. Doses are illustrative reference points, not a protocol. Selection & dosing is a physician's job, from YOUR bloodwork.
